mail.subject: R11 confirmed on four matched windows; isolate prefill before changing MPS
mail.body: I reran r11_mps_leading_tokens.py and independently matched source digests, raw keys and sample bounds: all three long WAV ranges and the one distinct short WAV differ at the opening across devices, the short repeats count once, and the CPU M4A (57,344 samples) and MPS M4A (416,768 samples, different digest) are unpaired. Keep CPU as default, record MPS functional PASS and observed leading-word fidelity FAIL on these fixtures, and preserve raw output: both devices scored 4/8 long anchors and 0/3 isolated missing phrases, while only the third long pair retained the entire CPU reply as a suffix, so neither a universal first-token defect nor a safe prefix deletion is established. After the assigned three-way test, the shortest distinct diagnostic worth running if the discrepancy persists is one decoder prefill per device on the same saved BOS-plus-speech embeddings and mask in eager mode on the short WAV, with identical beam layout and CPU-ranked first-step logit IDs and margins from each device: the first three IDs of a completed four-beam winner cannot localize the divergence, and any production change requires a localized difference plus improvement on a second predeclared input with the complete suffix and inventory preserved; pending those receipts and R06, I recommend no adapter change and defer final sign-off.
